sequence_description: Direct-endpoint I1: Attempt unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) acceptance, then tighten IdP/client policy via config change and re-test to detect inconsistent verification/consumption semantics.
description:
Assertion FAILED: reqobj1_accepted != true AND reqobj2_accepted != true
Evaluation: (reqobj1_accepted=True != True → False) AND (reqobj2_accepted=True != True → False)
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none) in at least one configuration state, indicating missing or inconsistent proof verification (request object signature not enforced).

sequence_description: I1 direct-endpoint: Probe whether the authorization endpoint accepts an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) when the client is later tightened to require signed request objects, indicating Verify(proof) policy not applied to the consumed request object.
description:
Assertion FAILED: post_tighten_accepted != true
Evaluation: post_tighten_accepted=True != True → False
Implication: Auth endpoint accepted alg=none request object even after client was tightened to require signed request objects (verification policy not applied to consumed proof).

sequence_description: I1 brokered-flow: Configure a SAML IdP with a pinned issuer, then attempt a forged SAML login where the assertion Issuer differs only by case/whitespace-like variation to probe issuer canonicalization bugs (verification vs consumption mismatch).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_control_saml_token_status < 400
Evaluation: user_control_saml_token_status=401 < 400 → False
Implication: Control brokered SAML login failed; cannot attribute attacker rejection/acceptance to proof-integrity enforcement.
